note: Lyrics written from the Nervos Network RFCs, linked on each track. Vocals and music generated with the YuE2 song model; cover art with FLUX 3 Klein. Free to listen to and share for non-commercial use (YuE2 weights are CC BY-NC 4.0).

tracks.title: Scale It Up (2.1)
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Yeah, section two point one
How do you scale it up and let it run

[Verse]
Bitcoin came first, peer-to-peer cash
Ethereum followed with a general purpose stack
Both put a ceiling on what they can pack
Block size, gas limit, keep the nodes intact
You could pump the blocks up, let the fees stay low
Twenty-six gig blocks every ten minutes though
Petabyte a year, only data centres cope
Full nodes drop off, and there goes your hope
Rewards run dry when the last coin's mined
No fees, no miners, security declined
Can't verify yourself, gotta trust some firm
That ain't peer-to-peer, that's the lesson we learn

[Chorus]
Scale it up, don't sell it out
Keep the base layer strong, no doubt
Settle on the chain, move the rest off
Layer one holds it down, layer two takes off
Scale it up, don't sell it out
One global state, that's what it's about

[Verse]
Split it into shards, many chains in a row
Local consensus fast, beacon chain says go
Polkadot's parachains, relay in the middle
But a cross-shard call turns a deal to a riddle
Book a train and a hotel, both gotta go through
Two shards out of sync, now what you gonna do
Yank the contract over, leave a hole behind
DeFi building blocks get hard to combine
One plus N, the meta-chain's got a cap
Composability is where the value's at
Shards work fine when the apps stand alone
But the state worth most wants a single home

[Chorus]
Scale it up, don't sell it out
Keep the base layer strong, no doubt
Settle on the chain, move the rest off
Layer one holds it down, layer two takes off
Scale it up, don't sell it out
One global state, that's what it's about

[Verse]
Layer two, the base chain settles the score
Proofs fly off-chain, instant, cost no more
Alice gets a coffee every morning on the block
Opens up a channel, puts a deposit in stock
Signs a little slip every time she takes a cup
Either side can close it and collect what's up
State channels carry any state you choose
Side-chains run fast but there's trust to lose
Plasma roots its trust in the main chain's floor
Operator goes rogue, you walk out the door
Only the disputes and the settlements land
Decentralised, secure, and it scales as planned

[Chorus]
Scale it up, don't sell it out
Keep the base layer strong, no doubt
Settle on the chain, move the rest off
Layer one holds it down, layer two takes off
Scale it up, don't sell it out
One global state, that's what it's about

[Outro]
Section two point one, that's the plan
Keep it on the base, scale it where you can

tracks.title: Who Pays the Guards
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Positioning paper, two point two point three
Who pays the guards when the rewards run free

[Verse]
Block size capped and the block time's fixed
So space gets scarce and the bidding begins
No loops in the script, so the length tells the cost
More inputs, more outputs, more fees get tossed
The value in the coin is a shared belief
A store of value, that's the whole motif
But the miners get paid in the coin they guard
So the faith has to hold or the fall comes hard
Make a U T X O, pay the fee one time
Then it sits in the state till the end of the line
Pay once, stay forever, that's a sweet little deal
While the miners keep spending just to keep it real

[Chorus]
Who pays the guards when the rewards run dry
City gets rich, gotta fortify
Security budget gotta rise with the prize
Or the walls come down right before your eyes

[Verse]
Hard cap on the supply, the reward goes to zero
Then the fees alone gotta play the hero
Price goes double with rewards in the mix
Hash rate doubles, that's a natural fix
But fees don't care what the coin is worth
They follow block demand, for better or worse
You'd need full blocks every day of the year
And a fee that scales with the price, that's clear
Those are strong assumptions, put it on the list
And there's one more problem that you can't dismiss
Empty mempool and a block full of fees
A miner wants to fork it and take what he sees
Fee sniping, yeah, and it's still not solved
Not without the hard cap getting dissolved

[Chorus]
Who pays the guards when the rewards run dry
City gets rich, gotta fortify
Security budget gotta rise with the prize
Or the walls come down right before your eyes

[Outro]
Good for payments, but for holding it's thin
That's the puzzle that the paper steps in

tracks.title: Propose, Then Commit
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Four point two, consensus on the floor
Nakamoto's good but we're asking for more

[Verse]
Nakamoto consensus, simple and lean
Low overhead, it's a beautiful machine
Two drawbacks though that you can't ignore
Throughput's slow and there's a selfish mining door
So we watch the orphan rate across the net
How well it's connected is the reading we get
Orphans stay low, let the difficulty drop
Blocks come faster and the bandwidth pops
Orphans climb high, pull the pace back down
Every bit of bandwidth gets used in this town

[Chorus]
Propose, then commit, two steps on the beat
Propose, then commit, no bottleneck heat
Count every uncle when you tune the grind
Selfish mining gets left behind

[Verse]
The bottleneck's the block as it moves on the wire
So we split confirmation and the latency's retired
First you propose in the proposal zone
Then you commit in a window that's known
By the time that the block comes knocking at the gate
Every node's seen the transactions, no wait
Now the selfish miner orphans blocks for a gain
Because difficulty never counted that pain
Put the uncles in the difficulty sum
Any mix of strategies, the profit is none
Short attack window from the two-step flow
De facto selfish mining got nowhere to go

[Chorus]
Propose, then commit, two steps on the beat
Propose, then commit, no bottleneck heat
Count every uncle when you tune the grind
Selfish mining gets left behind

[Outro]
Short block interval, security intact
Throughput up, and that's a matter of fact

tracks.title: Do the Work
tracks.source: RFC 1 §4.2.4 Proof of Work vs Proof of Stake
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Four point two point four
Work versus stake, settle the score

[Verse]
Both of them bend to concentrated power
But look how they live in the day to day hour
Proof of work burns real world expense
Slip on your costs and you're over the fence
Gotta innovate, gotta build, gotta spend
Hardware, pools, cheap power to the end
Three things to corner, and they all keep moving
Hard to hold a monopoly when tech keeps improving
Proof of stake pays by the size of the pile
Low cost to run it, just sit there and smile
First mover edge only grows with the scale
A few big stakers and the balance goes pale

[Chorus]
Open door, no permission to ask
Layer one's got one main task
Decentralised, secure, and neutral ground
Do the work, that's how the chain stays sound

[Verse]
Validators hold one power that's unique
They decide who joins, and they don't have to speak
Censor a transaction, shuffle the line
Hard to detect and it's hard to fine
Proof of work's open, come as you are
Early birds get no head start in this bar
They say staking pulls demand for the coin
True at the start while the stakers all join
Then the rate goes flat, in and out the same
Staking by itself is no long term game
Long term holders got three ways to roll
Run a node, or delegate and give up control
Or sit there diluted while the new coins drop
None of that's sweet for the store of value shop

[Chorus]
Open door, no permission to ask
Layer one's got one main task
Decentralised, secure, and neutral ground
Do the work, that's how the chain stays sound

[Outro]
Stake's got a role in the economy, sure
But the base of it all needs an open door

tracks.title: Eaglesong
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Hey, party people, gather round
Let me tell you 'bout a brand new hashing sound
Eaglesong, y'all, Eaglesong

[Verse]
Any node can propose, here's the deal
The block's gotta be valid and the puzzle's gotta be real
The puzzle's tied to the block you bring
So the answer names the block, that's a one of one thing
Bitcoin hashes with a double S H A
Good for them back in the day
But the world built machines for it stack on stack
And a whole lot of them just sit out back
New coin, same hash, and those boxes wake
Rent the hash power, that's a risk to take
Can't predict who's mining, it could swing on a dime
So you want a function that is new this time

[Chorus]
Novel, simple, and secure
Three design goals, that's for sure
Eaglesong, sing it loud
A brand new hash for a brand new crowd

[Verse]
New means nobody tuned it before
No head start waiting at the hardware store
Simple so the chips come easy to build
In the long run, dedicated hardware's a shield
Security's third, and you need a strong case
A hidden weak spot gives one miner the race
So here's how it's made, now follow along
Sponge construction, like Keccak's song
With a permutation out of A R X
Addition, rotation, and xor is next
Wide trail strategy backs the proof
Same one holding up the A E S roof

[Chorus]
Novel, simple, and secure
Three design goals, that's for sure
Eaglesong, sing it loud
A brand new hash for a brand new crowd

[Outro]
First of its kind with all three in one
Eaglesong, y'all, and the party's begun

tracks.title: Land and Houses
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Four point five, the economy
C K Bytes, come and ride with me

[Verse]
One C K Byte is a byte of the state
Hold a thousand, get a thousand, that's the going rate
Make one cell or split it into more
Capacity's the space that you're paying for
Store your data and the bytes get tied
Can't put them in the Dao while they're occupied
That's the cost that you carry, and it's priced by the street
So you free up the state when the price gets steep
Let it go and the bytes come back
Same size as the data that you had in the stack

[Chorus]
Land and houses, land and houses
Bytes are the land, your assets are houses
State rent ticking while you occupy
Lock it in the Dao and the rent slides by

[Verse]
Genesis block, thirty-three point six bill
Eight point four burned and it's burning still
Base issuance halves every four years
All to the miners till the reward disappears
Secondary issuance, steady every year
One point three four four billion, clear
Nervos Dao is the shelter from the rain
Deposit and the dilution's just a name
Hold it like a hard cap, that's the long term play
But the bytes in a cell are the ones that pay
Proportional to space and proportional to time
Not pay once and sit there till the end of the line
Miners get the base and a slice of the second
Sized by the state that's in use, as reckoned
When the base runs out there's still rent to earn
Tied to adoption, not the fee market's turn

[Chorus]
Land and houses, land and houses
Bytes are the land, your assets are houses
State rent ticking while you occupy
Lock it in the Dao and the rent slides by

[Outro]
Demand for many assets into one flows through
And it pays for the guards, that's the point of view

tracks.title: Generate Here, Verify There
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
R F C two, four point one
Generate here, verify there, and done

[Verse]
Split the work in two, that's the first design
Generate the state off-chain, verify on the line
Same algorithm, two places to run
Client side builds it, the C K B V M checks it's done
Old state plus input makes a new state fresh
Pack it in a transaction, send it to the mesh
Nodes run it back with the same two things
If the output matches, then the new state sings

[Chorus]
Generate off-chain, verify on
You know the result before the transaction's gone
It passes or it fails, no in between
Certain every time, that's the whole machine

[Verse]
Deterministic, you can see what you made
Before you broadcast, no surprise gets played
Inputs and outputs, written in plain
So nodes see what depends on what in the chain
That means parallel, side by side they go
Workload gets spread and the system don't slow
Pick any language on the client that you please
Fast to develop and it runs with ease
Sometimes the checking is the cheaper deal
Quicksort's N log N to build for real
But checking that it's sorted is a single pass
Binary search, log N, verify in a flash
The more complex the rules, the wider the gap
And that asymmetry is throughput on tap
Zero knowledge proofs fit right in the frame
Generators off-chain is what we call that game

[Chorus]
Generate off-chain, verify on
You know the result before the transaction's gone
It passes or it fails, no in between
Certain every time, that's the whole machine

[Outro]
Details stay with you, privacy's a gain
Only the proof goes down on the chain

tracks.title: Four Fields in a Cell
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Yes yes y'all, and you don't stop
Four fields in a cell, now watch it drop

[Verse]
Capacity, that's the size limit, friend
Everything inside has to fit in the end
Data is the state that you put in the cell
Could be empty, but it's under the limit as well
Type is the script that checks the state
Lock is the script that guards the gate
Lock says who owns it, who can pass it along
Type says the rules so the data ain't wrong

[Chorus]
Capacity, data, type, and lock
Four fields in a cell, now rock
Live cells now, dead cells then
Use it one time and you make it again

[Verse]
A cell can't change, it's set like stone
Used one time, and one time alone
Want an update, here's what you do
Old one's history, you make a new
Same capacity, and it swaps in one go
Old state out, new state in the flow
All the live cells are the knowledge today
All the dead cells are the history, okay
Got ten bytes, you can split it in two
Five and five, now there's more for you
Type runs when the cell is made
Lock runs when it's spent or it's traded
Bring your proof, and if the lock says true
Then the type script rules what you get to do

[Chorus]
Capacity, data, type, and lock
Four fields in a cell, now rock
Live cells now, dead cells then
Use it one time and you make it again

[Verse]
No hard coded crypto in the V M
Bring your own signature, any kind of them
Multisig, M of N, easy to write
Lend out a cell and keep ownership tight
U T X O's clear but the scripts are thin
Account model's easy but the parallel's grim
Cell takes the best of both, you see
A generic state model for you and me

[Chorus]
Capacity, data, type, and lock
Four fields in a cell, now rock
Live cells now, dead cells then
Use it one time and you make it again

tracks.title: Space and Time
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Section five, where the state gets priced
Space and time, yeah, think about it twice

[Verse]
Making new state means the nodes gotta check
Storing that state means disk on their neck
Other chains charge you one time at the door
Then you sit on every node forevermore
Here the cell is the unit, and it's one at a time
Use the space yourself and the interest ain't mine
Could've lent it out, could've earned on the side
That's the cost that you carry for the space you occupied
Bigger and longer means the more you pay
Implicit, no bill coming day by day
No upfront rent that runs out on the clock
No state recycled and a contract in shock

[Chorus]
Space and time, space and time
You pay for the state in space and time
Not computation, it's the state that counts
Capacity holds it in the right amounts

[Verse]
Capacity, type, and lock are state as well
Metadata costs you in every cell
So you make fewer cells and you keep it tight
Capacity efficient, yeah, that's right
Change the data or move who owns
That's a fee, and the miners set the tones
Cycles used and the state you changed
Market finds the price in a healthy range
Cell owners cover fees for the folks they serve
New users walk in with no learning curve
Pay with capacity, that's the native one
Or a user-defined asset if the miner says done
No hard coded payment in the transaction, see
Because the model is the state, not the fee
Forcing native coin is a wall at the gate
Take it down and adoption don't wait

[Chorus]
Space and time, space and time
You pay for the state in space and time
Not computation, it's the state that counts
Capacity holds it in the right amounts

[Outro]
Secure common knowledge, hold it long
That's the main job, and the fee's just a song

tracks.title: Risk Five
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
R F C three, the virtual machine
Risk five underneath, keep it clean

[Verse]
The V M's job is to validate
Inputs and outputs, is the transaction straight
Built on risk five, sixty-four bit core
Multiply and divide, then a little bit more
Compressed instructions keep the contract small
No floating point in the set at all
Need a float, pack a soft float in
Deterministic is the way we win
The contract format is a Linux elf
Every tool you know, right there on the shelf

[Chorus]
Main returns zero, that's a pass
Sixty-four bit risk five, built to last
Four megs of memory, single thread
Count every cycle, like the paper said

[Verse]
Four megabytes is the runtime space
Code pages, stack, and the heap in place
Plus the mapped pages from another cell
Runs like a program on a single core shell
Starts at main with arg c and arg v
Return a zero and success is the decree
Might just hand you metadata there
Then syscalls load the rest with care
Single threaded, strict, no atomics required
Bring your own coroutines if that's desired
Any language with a risk five back end
C or Rust, compile it and send
Compile a whole V M, load it as a cell
Run JavaScript or Ruby as well
Cost is the cycles, instruction by instruction
Plus the cells that you read in the function

[Chorus]
Main returns zero, that's a pass
Sixty-four bit risk five, built to last
Four megs of memory, single thread
Count every cycle, like the paper said

[Outro]
Low level machine and it don't pretend
Real hardware rules from beginning to end

tracks.title: Write or Execute
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
Write or execute, pick a side
One or the other, nowhere to hide

[Verse]
No M M U in the C K B V M
Like the early C P Us, way back when
Whole block of memory, read, write, and run
Nothing stops a script changing code for fun
Jump to the stack and pretend it's code
That's a wide open door on a dangerous road
Buffer overflow goes writing on the text
Now the script's behaviour is whatever comes next
And the V M itself gets harder to make
Trace cache needs guarding on every write you take
Error prone and it's slow to boot
So here comes a rule to cut it at the root

[Chorus]
Write or execute, never both
Every page takes a single oath
Break the rule and you catch a fault
Write or execute, that's the vault

[Verse]
Four K pages, aligned on the line
Zero, then four K, eight K, every time
Each page carries a flag for the two
Writable or executable, one will do
Before an instruction, check the page can run
Before a write, check the page allows one
Break either rule and a page fault lands
That's the law, and that's how it stands
On boot every page starts writable, then
The load sections marked to execute, amen
An elf with a section that's both gets denied
Returns with an error, no free ride
Code not aligned, stretch it to the edge
Round to the page, that's the pledge
Return oriented tricks could still get through
But the easy mistakes get stopped for you

[Chorus]
Write or execute, never both
Every page takes a single oath
Break the rule and you catch a fault
Write or execute, that's the vault

[Outro]
Simpler machine and a safer script
And the just in time compiler's better equipped

tracks.title: Headers First
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
R F C four, how the blocks come in
Headers first, let the sync begin

[Verse]
Three stages, and they go in a row
Cheapest check first, that's the way to go
Connect the header, check the format and the work
Five percent effort for a ninety-five perk
Then download the block and check it's whole
Then accept it in the chain, that's the final goal
A block starts unknown before the header's read
Fail any step and it's invalid instead
Connected, downloaded, accepted at last
Never ahead of the parent in the past
If the parent goes bad then the children go too
So you don't waste work on a branch that's through

[Chorus]
Connect the header, download the block
Accept it in the chain, tick tock
Headers first, least cost on top
Most work wins, and the sync don't stop

[Verse]
Alice meets Bob and she samples her chain
Latest ten blocks, then she steps back again
Two, four, eight, with the gaps getting wide
That's the locator, sends it to his side
Bob finds the block that they both agree
Sends the headers from there to his tip, you see
Same genesis, so there's always one
Now the downloading stage can run
Sliding window, split it into stripes
Scheduled over peers with the right block types
Merkle root wrong, don't call the block bad
Blacklist the sender, that's the peer you had
Or a liar could poison your status tree
Then accept with the context, the heavy degree
Roll back the tip and verify the line
If it fails, restore the best chain, fine

[Chorus]
Connect the header, download the block
Accept it in the chain, tick tock
Headers first, least cost on top
Most work wins, and the sync don't stop

[Outro]
Tip moves on, so announce it to the crew
Compact block if there's one, headers if a few

tracks.title: Machine Mode
tracks.lyrics:
[Intro]
R F C five, the privileged mode
Opt in only, it's off in the code

[Verse]
One contract at a time, so you don't need rings
But a privileged model brings a few good things
An M M U for the contracts that grow
Dynamic memory, and the bad access? No
Beginners trade cycles for a safer run
Pros who want it lean can leave it undone
Closed by default, it's your call to make
Ignore it completely for the cycles' sake

[Chorus]
Machine mode, user mode
Two levels in the privileged code
M ret, and you step on down
Sixty-four entries when the fault comes round

[Verse]
C S R instructions, straight from the spec
Read and write registers, keep it correct
Not every register, just the ones for the trap
S T vec holds the handler on the map
Touch the others, illegal instruction's the call
Handle it how you like, that's all
Starts in machine mode, free to roam
User mode's limited, a smaller home
No C S R, no machine mode page
No executing where the flag's not engaged
Set your metadata up, then drop with M ret
Now the trap function's what catches the threat

[Verse]
T L B, sixty-four entries deep
Each one a page, four K to keep
One way associative, here's the trick
Same last six bits and one gets kicked
Switch your privilege level, the whole thing's flushed
Built on the first page fault, never rushed
Stay in machine mode, you may never meet
Once it's up, it stays on the beat

[Chorus]
Machine mode, user mode
Two levels in the privileged code
M ret, and you step on down
Sixty-four entries when the fault comes round

[Outro]
Opt in, opt out, it's yours to decide
The V M's got it waiting on the side
